Expectation1: Respond to emails and messages within a reasonable time frame
Situation1: Leadership needs a prompt reply to confirm details for an external partner.
Expectation2: Challenge unfair systems and influence policy change
Situation2: They gather recurring cases of unfair treatment and bring them to discussions with community leaders or officials.
Story: My phone buzzed with a new email from our department head, marked urgent. The leadership team needed my confirmation on a project detail before they could finalize an agreement with an external partner. As a colleague, I knew how important it was to respond quickly—everyone was counting on me to keep things moving smoothly. But just as I started typing my reply, my phone lit up again with a message from a community member. She described another instance of unfair treatment, echoing the same patterns I’d been documenting for weeks. As an advocate, I felt a deep responsibility to gather these stories and bring them to the next meeting with local officials. Both roles demanded my immediate attention: my team needed my efficiency, but the community needed my voice. My fingers hovered over the keyboard, my mind torn between the urgent needs of my colleagues and the pressing call to challenge the system. The weight of both expectations pressed down on me, and I could feel my heart racing as I tried to decide which role to answer first.
